title: Steering Wheel Torque Sensor Malfunction
shortDescription: The electric power steering torque sensor has reported a fault.
fullDescription: The torque sensor measures driver input force on the steering wheel and is critical for electric power steering (EPS) assist calculation. A malfunction disables or limits power assist, requiring substantially more effort to steer.
safetyImpact: Loss of power steering assist or stability control; significantly increased steering effort and reduced vehicle control in emergencies.

causes.cause: Failed sensor, motor, or control module

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bidirectional scan tool to read codes from EPS, ABS, and BCM. Note any related codes and freeze frame.

fixSteps.title: Verify Battery and Charging
fixSteps.instruction: EPS systems are sensitive to voltage. Confirm battery is healthy and charging system delivers spec voltage under load.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring and Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check the EPS harness, column connectors, and power feed for corrosion, damage, or loose pins. Repair as needed.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate or Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: If calibration is required, perform the steering angle / torque sensor zero-point procedure. If a sensor or module has failed, replace and re-calibrate.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with this code?
faq.a: Drive with extreme caution. Steering effort may be much higher than normal, especially at low speeds. Have the system diagnosed promptly.

faq.q: Can I clear this code myself?
faq.a: Clearing without repair will not fix the issue. Many EPS faults also require a calibration procedure with a capable scan tool.

faq.q: Will my insurance or warranty cover this?
faq.a: EPS components are often covered under powertrain or comprehensive warranties. Check with your dealer or insurer for specifics.

fullDescription: Lock pin remains engaged when ignition is on. Vehicle cannot be steered. Often requires lock module replacement.
safetyImpact: Loss of power steering assist or stability control; significantly increased steering effort and reduced vehicle control in emergencies.

causes.cause: Failed sensor, motor, or control module

fixSteps.title: Scan All Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a bidirectional scan tool to read codes from EPS, ABS, and BCM. Note any related codes and freeze frame.

fixSteps.title: Verify Battery and Charging
fixSteps.instruction: EPS systems are sensitive to voltage. Confirm battery is healthy and charging system delivers spec voltage under load.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring and Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check the EPS harness, column connectors, and power feed for corrosion, damage, or loose pins. Repair as needed.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate or Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: If calibration is required, perform the steering angle / torque sensor zero-point procedure. If a sensor or module has failed, replace and re-calibrate.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with this code?
faq.a: Drive with extreme caution. Steering effort may be much higher than normal, especially at low speeds. Have the system diagnosed promptly.

faq.q: Can I clear this code myself?
faq.a: Clearing without repair will not fix the issue. Many EPS faults also require a calibration procedure with a capable scan tool.

faq.q: Will my insurance or warranty cover this?
faq.a: EPS components are often covered under powertrain or comprehensive warranties. Check with your dealer or insurer for specifics.
